summary: Customer wants to investigate a fiber-based measurement closer to a petroleum process for water determination, with the analyzer outside the process area, before selecting equipment. They ask what to clarify and what a first comparison experiment should establish.

facts_stated.text: Samples are currently sent to a laboratory for water determination.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: send samples to a laboratory for water determination

facts_stated.text: The analyzer would be outside the process area.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area.

customer_premises.claim: A fiber-based measurement closer to the process will allow changes to be noticed sooner.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: fiber based measurement closer to the process so that changes can be noticed sooner

customer_premises.claim: The analyzer can be located outside the process area while still measuring the process stream.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area.

unknowns: Target species concentration range and required detection limit for water.
Petroleum stream matrix composition, phase state, and possible interferents.
Physical state and optical behaviour of the stream at the measurement point.
Process temperature, pressure, flow, and installation constraints.
Required measurement accuracy, precision, and response time for detecting changes.
Reference laboratory method details and sampling procedure.
Fiber type, optical method, and whether any fluorescent indicator is intended.
Cleaning, fouling, and maintenance requirements for the process interface.
Exact installation point and distance between process and analyzer.
